Definition: adverb from a derivative of ῥοῖζος (a whir); whizzingly, i.e. with a crash:--with a great noise.
BiblicalUsage: The day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night, in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that the great noise is the sound of a world being unmade, and the day will come whether men listen for it or not.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
